summary: You had knee surgery on June 6, 2026, at Pacific Coast Surgery Center. The main surgery (line L1) was mostly covered by your plan. A second service on the same day (ultrasound guidance, line L2) was bundled into the surgery cost, so the provider cannot bill you separately for it. You owe $580 for coinsurance on the main surgery.

lines.explanation: Knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy (CPT 29881). The provider billed $6,800, but your plan's allowed amount is $2,900. The plan paid $2,320. You owe $580 in coinsurance, which is your percentage share of the allowed amount. [CODE-PR-2: "PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met."] The difference between what was billed ($6,800) and the allowed amount ($2,900) is written off by the provider as a contractual adjustment. [CODE-CO-45: "Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care."]

citations.quote: PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met.
Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care.

lines.explanation: Ultrasound guidance during procedure (CPT 76942). This service is bundled into the main surgery performed the same day. [CODE-CO-97: "CO-97 means payment for this service is included in the payment for another service performed the same day, a practice called bundling. The provider cannot separately bill the member for a bundled service."] The provider's $450 charge is written off and you owe nothing for this line.

citations.quote: CO-97 means payment for this service is included in the payment for another service performed the same day, a practice called bundling. The provider cannot separately bill the member for a bundled service.

actions: Verify that you have not received a separate bill from Pacific Coast Surgery Center for the ultrasound guidance (CPT 76942). If you have, contact the provider and reference CO-97 bundling code to dispute the charge.
Review your plan documents to confirm the coinsurance percentage (the plan appears to have paid 80% and you pay 20% of the allowed amount).
Verify that the $580 coinsurance charge matches your plan's stated out-of-pocket cost-sharing rules.
